summary: This article explains what a border is, how countries typically decide where a border lies using natural features or agreed-upon lines, and why border checkpoints exist.
introduce: Read the title “Borders: Lines That Divide Countries” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: a line that shows where one area or territory ends and another begins
an area of land that belongs to or is controlled by a particular country
to talk with another side in order to reach an agreement

challengeTerms.def: to mark out or set the exact limits of something, such as a border
having full, independent authority to govern a territory
the buildings, roads, and systems a government sets up to support an activity

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a border is just an imaginary line, so it does not really matter where it is drawn? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain two different ways that countries can decide where a border lies.
struggling: Pre-teach boundary, territory, and negotiate with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use demarcate, sovereign, and infrastructure in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
